title: Test Connection only checks TCP reachability — passes with wrong credentials or a non-SSH service
existing_state: The grid right-click "Test connection" feature (Form1.cs:8875-8947, 5-way concurrent, paints per-cell pass/fail) calls SshExecutionService.TestConnectionAsync which is a raw TcpClient connect-and-close (SshExecutionService.cs:2304-2339; the comment at 2300-2303 says this is deliberate "since hosts may not be SSH servers"). It therefore shows green for any open port 22 — a captive portal, a telnet listener, or an SSH server that will reject the user's credentials or key algorithms. Authentication failures, algorithm-mismatch fallback (the three-tier ladder at 2365+), and per-host credential resolution problems (vault_path, Credential Manager, ssh-config) are only discovered mid-run, host by host, during a real execution.
recommendation: Add a second test tier — e.g., a "Test SSH login" item next to the existing TCP test — that reuses the production connect path (CreateConnectedClientWithFallback + the same key/password login used in ExecuteSingleHost) with the same per-host credential resolution as a real run, then disconnects immediately. Return a richer ConnectionTestResult distinguishing Port-open / SSH-negotiated / Authenticated, and on failure include the already-built negotiation diagnostics (AppendSshNegotiationDiagnostics, SshExecutionService.cs:2628) in the cell tooltip.
user_benefit: Lets the user validate credentials and SSH compatibility across the whole fleet in seconds before a change window, instead of discovering auth failures one timeout at a time during the actual run.

evidence.note: TestConnectionAsync is TcpClient connect/close only, by design comment
UI test feature: concurrency-limited per-row test painting cell states — natural place for an SSH-tier mode
Production fallback connect path and negotiation diagnostics already exist for reuse in a real SSH test

mockup_idea: Host grid cells with a three-state indicator after test: gray dot 'port open', blue dot 'SSH OK', green check 'login OK'; a failed row shows a red X with tooltip 'Authentication failed for admin (password rejected)'.
